title: First Adult Case of Echovirus 21–Associated Poliomyelitis-Like Myelitis Presenting with Flaccid Asymmetric Tetraparesis
abstract: Abstract Background Non-polio enterovirus–associated myelitis is a rare condition causing acute flaccid paralysis due to anterior horn cell injury. While most cases occur in children, reports in adults are exceedingly uncommon. Methods We report the first known case in a 63-year-old woman with relapsed/refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) after second-line therapy with rituximab and ibrutinib. Following leukapheresis for planned CAR-T-cell therapy, she received bridging chemotherapy with bendamustine, cytarabine, and rituximab. During prolonged neutropenia and lymphopenia, she developed sudden asymmetric tetraparesis. Diagnostic workup included brain and spinal MRI, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis with cytology and flow cytometry, nerve conduction studies (NCS), and electromyography (EMG). Results NCS and EMG demonstrated a predominantly axonal neuropathy with acute denervation. Spinal MRI revealed cervical intramedullary T2 hyperintensities with a characteristic “snake-eye” sign involving the anterior horns. CSF analysis showed normal cell counts and protein levels without lymphoma involvement. Multiplex PCR detected enteroviruses, subsequently identified as Echovirus-21. Initial treatment with intravenous immunoglobulins for suspected Guillain–Barré syndrome was discontinued after confirmation of enterovirus-associated myelitis, and supportive care was provided. Discussion Although rare in adults, enterovirus-associated myelitis should be considered in immunosuppressed patients presenting with acute flaccid paralysis. Early diagnosis using spinal MRI, CSF PCR, and electrodiagnostic studies is essential to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 非脊髓灰质炎肠道病毒相关性脊髓炎是一种罕见疾病,由于前角细胞损伤而导致急性弛缓性麻痹。虽然大多数病例发生在儿童中,但成人的报道却极为罕见。方法 我们报告了首例已知病例,患者为一名 63 岁女性,在接受利妥昔单抗和依鲁替尼二线治疗后患有复发/难治性套细胞淋巴瘤 (MCL)。在计划进行 CAR-T 细胞治疗的白细胞分离术后,她接受了苯达莫司汀、阿糖胞苷和利妥昔单抗的桥接化疗。在长期中性粒细胞减少和淋巴细胞减少期间,她突然出现不对称性四肢轻瘫。诊断检查包括脑部和脊髓 MRI、脑脊液 (CSF) 细胞学和流式细胞术分析、神经传导研究 (NCS) 和肌电图 (EMG)。结果 NCS 和 EMG 显示主要为轴突神经病变并伴有急性去神经支配。脊髓 MRI 显示颈髓内 T2 高信号,并伴有涉及前角的特征性“蛇眼”征。脑脊液分析显示细胞计数和蛋白质水平正常,没有淋巴瘤参与。多重 PCR 检测到肠道病毒,随后被鉴定为 Echovirus-21。最初使用 治疗 静脉注射免疫球蛋白治疗疑似格林-巴利综合征,在确认肠道病毒相关性脊髓炎后停止,并提供支持性护理。讨论 尽管在成人中罕见,但对于出现急性弛缓性麻痹的免疫抑制患者,应考虑肠病毒相关性脊髓炎。早期使用脊柱 MRI、CSF PCR 和电诊断研究的 诊断 对于避免误诊和不适当的 治疗 至关重要。

title: Enterovirus D68 infection causing plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia: a case report and literature review
abstract: Background Plastic bronchitis (PB) is a rare disease characterized by the formation of tree-like or tubular mucus plugs within the bronchi, which can lead to severe airway obstruction and respiratory failure, potentially becoming life-threatening if diagnosis and treatment are delayed. Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections in children,which can lead to wheezing, acute flaccid myelitis, and even respiratory failure. Nevertheless, a direct association between EV-D68 infection and plastic bronchitis has not been previously reported. As the first documented case, this report establishes the association between EV-D68 and plastic bronchitis, thereby expanding the clinical spectrum of EV-D68. Methods We report a case of plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia caused by Enterovirus D68 infection. To identify additional cases and elucidate the clinical characteristics of this condition, a systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases for the period from January 2006 to June 2026. The search strategy employed the following keywords: “Enterovirus D68” “plastic bronchitis” and “severe pneumonia”. Case description This case involved an 11-year-old girl with previously good health. Chief complaints: cough and wheezing for 1 day, chest pain for half a day. Chest CT showed patchy increased-density opacities in the left upper loben with reduced left upper lobe volume, small nodular increased-density opacities in the left lower lobe and right lower lobe, right pleural thickening. Following admission, two flexible bronchoscopic examinations with plastic cast removal and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were performed; bronchoscopic findings were consistent with plastic bronchitis and bronchial mucosal inflammation. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid(BALF) detected Enterovirus D68 and Rhinovirus. Intravenous immunoglobulin support and methylprednisolone anti-inflammatory therapy were also administered. By hospital day 10, the patient's condition had stabilized;Follow-up chest CT demonstrated resolution of the left upper lobe patchy high-density opacities with re-expansion of the left upper lobe, patchy high-density opacities in the left lower lobe and small left pleural effusion. The newly developed lesion in the left lower lobe was considered resolving inflammatory changes rather than new active infection. The patient was discharged with medication. At 6 days post-discharge, follow-up chest CT demonstrated complete resolution of pulmonary infiltrates, pleural effusions, consistent with full clinical recovery. The total duration of treatment was 10 days of hospitalization plus 6 days of oral therapy after discharge, giving a total of 16 days. Conclusion EV-D68 infection should be recognized as a potential etiology of plastic bronchitis or severe pneumonia in children. In addition to direct pathogen-mediated tissue injury, immune-mediated damage warrants careful consideration in the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Early bronchoscopic intervention combined with anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory therapy may prove critical in shortening the disease course and improving clinical outcomes.

title_zh: 肠道病毒D68感染引起塑料性支气管炎和重症肺炎:病例报告及文献综述
source_body_en: Background Plastic bronchitis (PB) is a rare disease characterized by the formation of tree-like or tubular mucus plugs within the bronchi, which can lead to severe airway obstruction and respiratory failure, potentially becoming life-threatening if diagnosis and treatment are delayed. Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections in children,which can lead to wheezing, acute flaccid myelitis, and even respiratory failure. Nevertheless, a direct association between EV-D68 infection and plastic bronchitis has not been previously reported. As the first documented case, this report establishes the association between EV-D68 and plastic bronchitis, thereby expanding the clinical spectrum of EV-D68. Methods We report a case of plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia caused by Enterovirus D68 infection. To identify additional cases and elucidate the clinical characteristics of this condition, a systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases for the period from January 2006 to June 2026. The search strategy employed the following keywords: “Enterovirus D68” “plastic bronchitis” and “severe pneumonia”. Case description This case involved an 11-year-old girl with previously good health. Chief complaints: cough and wheezing for 1 day, chest pain for half a day. Chest CT showed patchy increased-density opacities in the left upper loben with reduced left upper lobe volume, small nodular increased-density opacities in the left lower lobe and right lower lobe, right pleural thickening. Following admission, two flexible bronchoscopic examinations with plastic cast removal and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were performed; bronchoscopic findings were consistent with plastic bronchitis and bronchial mucosal inflammation. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid(BALF) detected Enterovirus D68 and Rhinovirus. Intravenous immunoglobulin support and methylprednisolone anti-inflammatory therapy were also administered. By hospital day 10, the patient's condition had stabilized;Follow-up chest CT demonstrated resolution of the left upper lobe patchy high-density opacities with re-expansion of the left upper lobe, patchy high-density opacities in the left lower lobe and small left pleural effusion. The newly developed lesion in the left lower lobe was considered resolving inflammatory changes rather than new active infection. The patient was discharged with medication. At 6 days post-discharge, follow-up chest CT demonstrated complete resolution of pulmonary infiltrates, pleural effusions, consistent with full clinical recovery. The total duration of treatment was 10 days of hospitalization plus 6 days of oral therapy after discharge, giving a total of 16 days. Conclusion EV-D68 infection should be recognized as a potential etiology of plastic bronchitis or severe pneumonia in children. In addition to direct pathogen-mediated tissue injury, immune-mediated damage warrants careful consideration in the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Early bronchoscopic intervention combined with anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory therapy may prove critical in shortening the disease course and improving clinical outcomes.
abstract_zh: 背景 塑性支气管炎 (PB) 是一种罕见疾病,其特征是支气管内形成树状或管状粘液栓,可导致严重气道阻塞和呼吸衰竭,如果 诊断 和 治疗 延迟,可能会危及生命。肠道病毒D68(EV-D68)是引起儿童急性呼吸道感染的常见病原体,可导致喘息、急性弛缓性脊髓炎,甚至呼吸衰竭。然而,此前尚未报道过 EV-D68 感染与塑料性支气管炎之间的直接关联。作为第一个有记录的病例,该报告确立了 EV-D68 与塑料性支气管炎之间的关联,从而扩大了 EV-D68 的临床范围。方法报告1例由肠道病毒D68感染引起的塑料性支气管炎和重症肺炎。为了识别更多病例并阐明该病的临床特征,我们使用 PubMed、Embase 和 Web of Science 数据库对 2006 年 1 月至 2026 年 6 月期间进行了系统文献检索。检索策略采用以下关键词:“肠道病毒 D68”、“塑料性支气管炎”和“重症肺炎”。病例描述 该病例涉及一名 11 岁女孩,此前身体健康。主诉:咳嗽喘息1天,胸痛半天。胸部CT显示左上叶斑片状密度增高,左上叶体积缩小,左下叶和右下叶小结节状密度增高,右侧胸膜增厚。入院后,进行了两次柔性支气管镜检查,包括塑料铸型去除和支气管肺泡灌洗(BAL);支气管镜检查结果与塑料性支气管炎和支气管粘膜炎症一致。支气管肺泡灌洗液(BALF)的靶向下一代测序(tNGS)检测到肠道病毒D68和鼻病毒。还给予静脉免疫球蛋白支持和甲基强的松龙抗炎治疗。到入院第10天,患者病情已稳定;后续胸部CT显示左上叶斑片状高密度混浊消退,左上叶重新扩张,左下叶斑片状高密度混浊和左侧少量胸腔积液。左下叶新出现的病变被认为是解决了炎症变化,而不是新的活动性感染。患者经药物治疗出院。出院后 6 天,随访胸部 CT 显示肺部浸润、胸腔积液完全消退,与临床完全康复一致。治疗的总持续时间为住院10天加上出院后口服治疗6天,总共16天。结论 EV-D68感染应被认为是儿童塑料性支气管炎或重症肺炎的潜在病因。除了直接病原体介导的组织损伤外,免疫介导的损伤还需要仔细考虑潜在的病理生理机制。早期支气管镜干预结合抗炎和免疫调节治疗可能对缩短病程和改善临床结果至关重要。

title: CATCH-EVseq, an Ultra-Sensitive Capture Assay to Monitor Human Enterovirus RNA
abstract: The detection of low-abundance viral RNA in chronic or persistent infections remains a major challenge in virology, constrained by the sensitivity and specificity of traditional methods. One such infection, chronic enterovirus (EV) infection, has been proposed as a potential underlying factor in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME), although this hypothesis remains debated. Supporting evidence for EVs as a viral trigger includes historical spatiotemporal overlaps between ME outbreaks and poliomyelitis epidemics, frequent reports of “flu-like” illness at disease onset, seasonal outbreaks patterns, and serological findings. To address the problem of EV detection, we developed CATCH-EVseq, an ultra-sensitive platform built on the CATCH framework. By integrating high-throughput sequencing with cDNA capture using 49,847 probes targeting 3410 EV genomes, CATCH-EVseq achieved a detection limit in artificially created samples as low as one copy in a microgram of RNA for two out of three biological replicates. Additionally, spike-in controls allow for rigorous validation of the capture and sequencing throughout the CATCH-EVseq procedure. When applied to a small number of blood samples from both ME patients and healthy controls, CATCH-EVseq detected no EV RNA, either in direct assays or after in vitro viral amplification. While these results do not support the presence of circulating EV RNA in the blood of individuals with ME, they do not rule out persistent infection in other tissues or organs. Critically, CATCH-EVseq establishes a robust, ultra-sensitive framework for future investigations of low-level EV persistence in biopsies, post-mortem tissues, or other clinical contexts where chronic enterovirus infection is suspected.

title_zh: CATCH-EVseq,一种用于监测 人肠道病毒 RNA 的超灵敏捕获分析
source_body_en: The detection of low-abundance viral RNA in chronic or persistent infections remains a major challenge in virology, constrained by the sensitivity and specificity of traditional methods. One such infection, chronic enterovirus (EV) infection, has been proposed as a potential underlying factor in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME), although this hypothesis remains debated. Supporting evidence for EVs as a viral trigger includes historical spatiotemporal overlaps between ME outbreaks and poliomyelitis epidemics, frequent reports of “flu-like” illness at disease onset, seasonal outbreaks patterns, and serological findings. To address the problem of EV detection, we developed CATCH-EVseq, an ultra-sensitive platform built on the CATCH framework. By integrating high-throughput sequencing with cDNA capture using 49,847 probes targeting 3410 EV genomes, CATCH-EVseq achieved a detection limit in artificially created samples as low as one copy in a microgram of RNA for two out of three biological replicates. Additionally, spike-in controls allow for rigorous validation of the capture and sequencing throughout the CATCH-EVseq procedure. When applied to a small number of blood samples from both ME patients and healthy controls, CATCH-EVseq detected no EV RNA, either in direct assays or after in vitro viral amplification. While these results do not support the presence of circulating EV RNA in the blood of individuals with ME, they do not rule out persistent infection in other tissues or organs. Critically, CATCH-EVseq establishes a robust, ultra-sensitive framework for future investigations of low-level EV persistence in biopsies, post-mortem tissues, or other clinical contexts where chronic enterovirus infection is suspected.

title: Temporal dynamics of the cerebrospinal fluid proteome in tick-borne encephalitis and enteroviral meningitis
abstract: Background Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a severe viral infection of the central nervous system (CNS), causing acute meningoencephalitis and often long-term neurocognitive sequelae. The lack of specific treatment for TBE highlights the need to improve understanding of disease mechanisms and identify novel biomarkers. Enteroviral meningitis is typically a milder infection of the CNS and rarely causes encephalitis.Objectives In this hypothesis-generating study, we aimed to characterise temporal changes in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteome in TBE and identify candidate biomarkers associated with pathophysiological mechanisms, disease severity, and neurocognitive outcome.Methods Patients with TBE, enteroviral meningitis, or aseptic meningoencephalitis of unknown origin were retrospectively included from a previously established cohort. CSF proteomes were analysed by label-free mass spectrometry, followed by differential protein expression analysis and functional annotation. Temporal proteome dynamics and protein associations with disease severity and neurocognitive outcome were assessed. Data are available via ProteomeXchange with identifier PXD077931.Results Proteomic analyses revealed alterations in proteins related to synaptic function, inflammatory pathways, the complement system, and the 14-3-3 protein family. Adrenomedullin was markedly increased in the late phase of TBE compared with enteroviral meningitis.Conclusion Temporal changes in the CSF proteome in TBE indicate a strong inflammatory response occurring in concert with lower levels of proteins related to synaptic function during the acute phase. These findings provide insights into the host response and pathogenesis of TBE and identify proteins of potential interest for future validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterise temporal changes in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteome in tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) and identify candidate biomarkers associated with disease mechanisms and outcomes. Using label-free mass spectrometry, the researchers analysed CSF proteomes and found alterations in proteins related to synaptic function, inflammatory pathways, the complement system, and the 14-3-3 protein family. Adrenomedullin was notably increased in the late phase of TBE compared to enteroviral meningitis. title_zh: 蜱传脑炎和肠病毒性脑膜炎脑脊液蛋白质组的时间动态
source_body_en: Background Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a severe viral infection of the central nervous system (CNS), causing acute meningoencephalitis and often long-term neurocognitive sequelae. The lack of specific treatment for TBE highlights the need to improve understanding of disease mechanisms and identify novel biomarkers. Enteroviral meningitis is typically a milder infection of the CNS and rarely causes encephalitis.Objectives In this hypothesis-generating study, we aimed to characterise temporal changes in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteome in TBE and identify candidate biomarkers associated with pathophysiological mechanisms, disease severity, and neurocognitive outcome.Methods Patients with TBE, enteroviral meningitis, or aseptic meningoencephalitis of unknown origin were retrospectively included from a previously established cohort. CSF proteomes were analysed by label-free mass spectrometry, followed by differential protein expression analysis and functional annotation. Temporal proteome dynamics and protein associations with disease severity and neurocognitive outcome were assessed. Data are available via ProteomeXchange with identifier PXD077931.Results Proteomic analyses revealed alterations in proteins related to synaptic function, inflammatory pathways, the complement system, and the 14-3-3 protein family. Adrenomedullin was markedly increased in the late phase of TBE compared with enteroviral meningitis.Conclusion Temporal changes in the CSF proteome in TBE indicate a strong inflammatory response occurring in concert with lower levels of proteins related to synaptic function during the acute phase. These findings provide insights into the host response and pathogenesis of TBE and identify proteins of potential interest for future validation.
abstract_zh: 背景 蜱传脑炎(TBE)是一种严重的中枢神经系统(CNS)病毒感染,可引起急性脑膜脑炎,并常常造成长期的神经认知后遗症。TBE 缺乏特定的 治疗 突出表明需要提高对疾病机制的理解并识别新的生物标志物。肠病毒性脑膜炎通常是一种较温和的中枢神经系统感染,很少引起脑炎。目的 在这项假设生成研究中,我们旨在描述 TBE 中脑脊液 (CSF) 蛋白质组的时间变化,并确定与病理生理机制、疾病严重程度和神经认知结果相关的候选生物标志物。方法追溯地包括先前建立的 队列研究。通过无标记质谱分析脑脊液蛋白质组,然后进行差异蛋白表达分析和功能注释。评估了时间蛋白质组动力学以及蛋白质与疾病严重程度和神经认知结果的关联。数据可通过 ProteomeXchange 获得,标识符为 PXD077931。结果蛋白质组学分析揭示了与突触功能、炎症途径、补体系统和 14-3-3 蛋白家族相关的蛋白质的变化。与肠病毒性脑膜炎相比,TBE后期的肾上腺髓质素显着增加。结论TBE中脑脊液蛋白质组的时间变化表明在急性期发生了强烈的炎症反应,同时与突触功能相关的蛋白质水平降低。这些发现提供了对 TBE 的 宿主 响应和 发病机制 的深入了解,并确定了未来验证可能感兴趣的蛋白质。

title: Intracellular SCARB2 mimicry overcomes decoy failure to broadly inhibit enteroviruses.
abstract: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) and coxsackievirus A16 (CV-A16) are leading causes of severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) with high childhood mortality and no specific antiviral therapy. SCARB2 is the essential uncoating receptor, yet extracellular SCARB2-Fc decoys fail to block infection, representing a decade-old paradox in enterovirus therapeutics. Here, we overcome this limitation by engineering RMP(R8), a cell-penetrating SCARB2 mimetic peptide comprising the minimal VP2-binding domain (W146-K166) fused to an octa-arginine transporter. RMP(R8) shows potent antiviral activity (EC50 = 0.156 μg/mL), outstanding safety (selectivity index > 2003), and excellent aqueous solubility, a critical asset for clinical translation. It broadly inhibits genetically divergent EV-A71 isolates and CV-A16 in intestinal and neural cells by blocking viral entry. In a lethal neonatal mouse model, RMP(R8) increases survival against EV-A71 and CV-A16 challenge in vivo. Intracellular receptor mimicry thus establishes a generalizable strategy for viruses refractory to extracellular intervention. RMP(R8) is a promising clinical candidate to address the unmet need for targeted anti-enterovirus treatment, and our findings redefine how to drug virus-receptor interactions that act inside cells.

Here, we overcome this limitation by engineering RMP(R8), a cell-penetrating SCARB2 mimetic peptide comprising the minimal VP2-binding domain (W146-K166) fused to an octa-arginine transporter. RMP(R8) shows potent antiviral activity (EC50 = 0.156 μg/mL), outstanding safety (selectivity index > 2003), and excellent aqueous solubility, a critical asset for clinical translation. It broadly inhibits genetically divergent EV-A71 isolates and CV-A16 in intestinal and neural cells by blocking viral entry. In a lethal neonatal mouse model, RMP(R8) increases survival against EV-A71 and CV-A16 challenge in vivo. Intracellular receptor mimicry thus establishes a generalizable strategy for viruses refractory to extracellular intervention. RMP(R8) is a promising clinical candidate to address the unmet need for targeted anti-enterovirus treatment, and our findings redefine how to drug virus-receptor interactions that act inside cells.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of developing antiviral therapies for EV-A71 and CV-A16, which are major causes of severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in children. The research introduces RMP(R8), a cell-penetrating SCARB2 mimetic peptide designed to overcome the limitations of extracellular SCARB2-Fc decoys. RMP(R8) demonstrates potent antiviral activity, high safety, and good solubility, making it a promising candidate for clinical use. The peptide effectively inhibits both EV-A71 and CV-A16 in various cell types by blocking viral entry, and it improves survival in a neonatal mouse model. The findings suggest that intracellular receptor mimicry could be a viable strategy for targeting viruses that resist extracellular interventions. However, the study's results are based on in vitro and animal models, and further research is needed to validate these findings in human trials.

title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies
abstract: Conspectus In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish enteroviral 2C as a tractable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development. Rather than relying solely on conventional phenotypic high-throughput screening, our initial studies focused on the rational optimization of reported 2C inhibitors identified from a drug-repurposing campaign. This strategy led to quinoline-based antivirals with substantially improved potency and selectivity against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), providing early medicinal chemistry insights into ligand recognition by enteroviral 2C and supporting the feasibility of chemically targeting this protein. Building on these findings, we subsequently developed pyrazolopyridine-based inhibitors, which evolved into one of the most potent classes of enteroviral 2C inhibitors reported to date. Mechanistic studies combining differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF), serial viral passage, reverse genetics, and molecular modeling supported direct engagement of a conserved allosteric pocket corresponding to the previously defined (S)-fluoxetine binding site. Structure-guided optimization led to Jun6504, a rationally designed 2C inhibitor with improved metabolic stability, favorable pharmacokinetic properties, and robust in vivo efficacy in a neonatal mouse model of EV-D68-induced paralysis. Collectively, these studies provided strong pharmacological validation of 2C as a therapeutically actionable antiviral target. In parallel, we recognized that the absence of direct, scalable biochemical assays was a major impediment to 2C-targeted antiviral discovery. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to establish enteroviral 2C as a viable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the development of antivirals targeting enteroviral 2C proteins, with a focus on enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), EV-A71, and coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3).
analysis.methods: The researchers employed a fluorescence polarization-based binding assay to monitor ligand engagement of the conserved allosteric pocket in enteroviral 2C proteins. They also used differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF), serial viral passage, reverse genetics, and molecular modeling to study the mechanism of action of 2C inhibitors.
analysis.main_results: The initial studies led to the development of quinoline-based antivirals with improved potency and selectivity against EV-D68. Subsequently, pyrazolopyridine-based inhibitors were developed, which became one of the most potent classes of enteroviral 2C inhibitors reported to date.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that enteroviral 2C can be a therapeutically actionable antiviral target, supported by pharmacological validation and the development of a scalable discovery platform.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for the development of clinically useful antivirals targeting enteroviral 2C proteins, which could lead to improved treatment options for enterovirus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on specific enteroviral strains and the absence of clinical trials, but the evidence is strong due to the integration of multiple methodologies and the validation of pharmacological properties in a neonatal mouse model.

analysis.summary_en: This study outlines the development of antiviral drugs targeting enteroviral 2C proteins, emphasizing the integration of medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, and assay innovation. The researchers focused on EV-D68, EV-A71, and CVB3, using a fluorescence polarization-based binding assay and structure-based virtual screening to identify potent inhibitors. Their findings demonstrate the feasibility of targeting 2C for antiviral therapy, supported by pharmacological validation in a neonatal mouse model. The study provides a framework for future drug discovery efforts but is limited by its focus on specific strains and lack of clinical data. The evidence is strong, with clear results and methodological validation.

title: Mapping the Global Trends and Knowledge of Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease: A Bibliometric and Visual Analysis from 2002 to 2022
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to analyze the research evolution process, hotspots, and trends of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) over the past 20 years and try to explore future development directions. Methods: Publications related to HFMD were extracted from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). Based on bibliometric analysis, the keywords toward the publications, countries, institutions, authors, journals and references in the field of HFMD were quantitatively and visually analyzed using VOSviewer and CiteSpace. Results: A total of 4,279 publications related to HFMD were published in 880 journals by 49,435 authors from 3,312 institutions in 93 countries/regions, with the number of publications on HFMD increasing over the past 20 years. The most productive and influential countries were China and the United States (USA). The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) was the most prolific institution, and Shih SR was the most productive author. The most common keywords were enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), HFMD, enterovirus, myocarditis, coxsackievirus B3 (CV-B3), coxsackievirus, vaccines, coxsackievirus A16 (CV-A16), antivirals, and inflammation. Moreover, research hotspots and trends shifted mainly from clinical symptoms, pathogenesis and epidemiology of HFMD to vaccine development, antiviral research, surveillance, and early warning. Conclusion: HFMD is a growing global public health concern. Our findings provide a systematic bibliometric mapping of the research landscape of HFMD over the past two decades, which may shed light on future development directions for researchers.

title_zh: 绘制手足口病的全球趋势和知识图谱:2002 年至 2022 年的文献计量和视觉分析
source_body_en: Objective: This study aimed to analyze the research evolution process, hotspots, and trends of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) over the past 20 years and try to explore future development directions. Methods: Publications related to HFMD were extracted from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). Based on bibliometric analysis, the keywords toward the publications, countries, institutions, authors, journals and references in the field of HFMD were quantitatively and visually analyzed using VOSviewer and CiteSpace. Results: A total of 4,279 publications related to HFMD were published in 880 journals by 49,435 authors from 3,312 institutions in 93 countries/regions, with the number of publications on HFMD increasing over the past 20 years. The most productive and influential countries were China and the United States (USA). The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) was the most prolific institution, and Shih SR was the most productive author. The most common keywords were enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), HFMD, enterovirus, myocarditis, coxsackievirus B3 (CV-B3), coxsackievirus, vaccines, coxsackievirus A16 (CV-A16), antivirals, and inflammation. Moreover, research hotspots and trends shifted mainly from clinical symptoms, pathogenesis and epidemiology of HFMD to vaccine development, antiviral research, surveillance, and early warning. Conclusion: HFMD is a growing global public health concern. Our findings provide a systematic bibliometric mapping of the research landscape of HFMD over the past two decades, which may shed light on future development directions for researchers.
abstract_zh: 【摘要】:目的:分析近20年来手足口病(HFMD)研究的进程、热点及趋势,并探讨未来的发展方向。方法:从 Web of Science 核心合集 (WoSCC) 中提取与 HFMD 相关的出版物。在文献计量分析的基础上,利用VOSviewer和CiteSpace对手足口病领域的出版物、国家、机构、作者、期刊和参考文献的关键词进行定量和可视化分析。结果:来自93个国家/地区3,312个机构的49,435名作者在880种期刊上发表了4,279篇与手足口病相关的出版物,近20年来手足口病的出版物数量不断增加。最具生产力和影响力的国家是中国和美国。中国科学院 (CAS) 是最多产的机构,施 SR 是最多产的作者。最常见的关键词是肠道病毒 A71 (EV-A71)、手足口病、肠道病毒、心肌炎、柯萨奇病毒 B3 (CV-B3)、柯萨奇病毒、疫苗、柯萨奇病毒 A16 (CV-A16)、抗病毒药物 和炎症。此外,研究热点和趋势主要从手足口病的临床症状、发病机制和流行病学转向疫苗开发、抗病毒药物研究、监测和预警。结论:手足口病是一个日益严重的全球公共卫生问题。我们的研究结果为过去二十年手足口病的研究格局提供了系统的文献计量图,这可能为研究人员未来的发展方向指明方向。

title: Invasive Enterovirus and Parechovirus Infections in Adults, Alberta, Canada, 2023–2025
abstract: We conducted a retrospective, population-based laboratory surveillance study during May 2023–December 2025 in Alberta, Canada, to characterize adult invasive enterovirus and parechovirus infections and to identify groups at high risk for those infections. Of 15,621 samples tested, 162 (1.0%) were virus positive, of which 51 (31.5%) samples from 39 patients indicated invasive infections. Cerebrospinal fluid, blood, and cardiac tissue were the most frequent virus-positive specimens. The invasive enterovirus and parechovirus incidence rate was 0.37 cases/100,000 person-years; rates were higher in patients 50 years of age (incidence rate ratio 8.2; p<0.001). The annual incidence rates were 0.20–0.56 cases/100,000 person-years; rates appeared higher in 2025 than in 2024 (incidence rate ratio 2.1; p = 0.11). Severe disseminated enterovirus infection occurred in 2 patients who received ocrelizumab. Continuous surveillance and ongoing optimization of enterovirus and parechovirus detection assays is essential for comprehensive public health tracking.

title: Enterovirus infections: main types related to clinical syndromes
abstract: This narrative review highlights recent advances in the understanding of enterovirus infections and the main enterovirus types associated with clinical syndromes, synthesizing current knowledge of type-specific manifestations. We searched PubMed®, Scientific Electronic Library Online (SciELO), and Virtual Health Library (VHL) for articles published between 2010 and 2025. The search used descriptors and/or keywords in Portuguese and English: “enterovirus infection disease”, “enterovirus infection genotypes”, “enterovirus infection pathogenic”, and “enterovirus clinical syndromes”, focusing on recent studies addressing enterovirus infections and the types most commonly associated with clinical syndromes. A total of 78 articles were selected for analysis. The review examined the distribution of enteroviruses by species, recommended clinical specimen types for diagnosis according to clinical presentation, and the major enterovirus types and their associated clinical syndromes. Numerous studies have demonstrated the epidemic potential and genetic diversity of enteroviruses, revealing patterns of endemic circulation. However, the mechanisms underlying the ability of a wide variety of enterovirus types to infect the same tissue remain poorly understood.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on non‐polio human enteroviruses (e.g., EV‐A71, EV‐D68, CV‐A6, CV‐A16, echoviruses) and their associated clinical syndromes such as enterovirus infection, aseptic meningitis and enteroviral meningitis.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A narrative review searched PubMed, SciELO and VHL for articles published 2010‐2025 and selected 78 articles for analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that enteroviruses exhibit species‐specific distribution and clinical syndromes, and that specimen types should be chosen according to clinical presentation, while also noting their epidemic potential and genetic diversity.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: A major evidence gap remains in understanding the mechanisms that allow diverse enterovirus types to infect the same tissue.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future work should prioritize defining specimen types for diagnosis, further characterize species distribution, and investigate the molecular mechanisms enabling broad tissue tropism.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review synthesizes recent knowledge on human enteroviruses, emphasizing non‐polio types such as EV‐A71, EV‐D68, CV‐A6, CV‐A16 and echoviruses and their linked clinical syndromes including enterovirus infection, aseptic meningitis and enteroviral meningitis. By searching PubMed, SciELO and VHL for 2010‐2025 publications, the authors identified 78 relevant articles. They report that enteroviruses display species‐specific distribution and diverse clinical manifestations, recommend selecting diagnostic specimens based on presentation, and highlight the organisms' epidemic potential and genetic diversity. However, the mechanisms allowing many enterovirus types to infect the same tissue remain poorly understood, indicating a key research gap. The review thus calls for focused studies on diagnostic specimen selection, detailed epidemiologic characterization, and mechanistic investigations of broad tissue tropism.

title: Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic model to predict pharmacokinetics of KY0467 in humans and guide dose selection in infants and children
abstract: Background Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) caused by enterovirus 71 (EV71) remains a severe threat to infants and young children, with no specific antiviral therapy currently available. KY0467 is a novel EV71‐targeting antiviral drug under clinical development, but clinical data are limited to healthy adults, and appropriate pediatric dosing regimens are urgently needed. Methods In this study, a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model was developed and validated in rats and beagles, extrapolated to humans, and verified using clinical pharmacokinetic (PK) data from healthy adults. The model was then scaled to infants (28 days–23 months) and children (2–5 years) using age‐dependent physiological parameters to predict effective doses matching adult exposure at 30 mg/day. Results Predicted plasma concentration‐time profiles agreed well with observed values, and all mean fold errors (MFE) for T max , C max , and AUC 0‐t were within 0.5‐ to 2‐fold. Population simulations identified effective doses of 0.5 mg/kg/day for infants and 9 mg/day for children. Conclusions In conclusion, the adult PBPK model of KY0467 was successfully developed and validated for the first time, and the extrapolated pediatric model could be used to predict pediatric dosing of KY0467, which will provide invaluable references for the design of future clinical trials and its rational use in the pediatric population.

title_zh: 基于生理学的药代动力学模型可预测 KY0467 在人体中的药代动力学并指导婴儿和儿童的剂量选择
source_body_en: Background Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) caused by enterovirus 71 (EV71) remains a severe threat to infants and young children, with no specific antiviral therapy currently available. KY0467 is a novel EV71‐targeting antiviral drug under clinical development, but clinical data are limited to healthy adults, and appropriate pediatric dosing regimens are urgently needed. Population simulations identified effective doses of 0.5 mg/kg/day for infants and 9 mg/day for children. Conclusions In conclusion, the adult PBPK model of KY0467 was successfully developed and validated for the first time, and the extrapolated pediatric model could be used to predict pediatric dosing of KY0467, which will provide invaluable references for the design of future clinical trials and its rational use in the pediatric population.
abstract_zh: 背景 由肠道病毒 71 型 (EV71) 引起的手足口病 (HFMD) 仍然对婴幼儿构成严重威胁,目前尚无特定的 抗病毒药物 治疗方法。KY0467是一种新型EV71靶向抗病毒药物药物,正在临床开发中,但临床数据仅限于健康成人,迫切需要合适的儿童给药方案。方法 在本研究中,开发了一种基于生理学的药代动力学 (PBPK) 模型,并在大鼠和比格犬中进行了验证,外推到人类,并使用健康成人的临床药代动力学 (PK) 数据进行了验证。然后使用年龄相关的生理参数将该模型扩展到婴儿(28 天至 23 个月)和儿童(2-5 岁),以预测与成人每天 30 毫克暴露量相匹配的有效剂量。结果 预测的血浆浓度-时间曲线与观察值非常吻合,T max 、C max 和 AUC 0-t 的所有平均倍数误差 (MFE) 均在 0.5 至 2 倍范围内。人群模拟确定婴儿的有效剂量为 0.5 毫克/公斤/天,儿童的有效剂量为 9 毫克/天。结论 综上所述,首次成功开发并验证了KY0467的成人PBPK模型,外推的儿科模型可用于预测KY0467的儿童剂量,为未来临床试验的设计及其在儿科人群中的合理使用提供宝贵的参考。

title: Valorization of Grifola frondosa processing by‐products: purification, structural characterization, and anti‐ EV71 bioactivity of a novel low‐molecular‐weight polysaccharide‐peptide
abstract: BACKGROUND: The large volume of supernatant generated during Grifola frondosa extraction is typically discarded, resulting in substantial resource waste and environmental pressure. Such agro-fungal processing by-products are rich in potentially bioactive macromolecules, but efficient recycling strategies and biofunctional verification remain limited. Meanwhile, safe natural antiviral ingredients for pediatric enterovirus infection are lacking. This study established a sustainable chromatographic bioprocess to recover a low-molecular-weight polysaccharide-peptide (LMWPP) from G. frondosa waste liquid, with the aims of achieving high-value circular utilization of fungal processing wastewater and exploring its anti-EV71 potential. RESULTS: Da possessed pyranose structures with α- and β-glycosidic bonds and consisted of multiple monosaccharides and leucine-dominant amino acids. Recovered LMWPP exerted marked anti-EV71 effects by mitigating cytotoxicity, inhibiting viral replication, downregulating VP1 mRNA expression, and alleviating cell apoptosis. Transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated its regulatory effects on the complement and coagulation cascades, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling, and oxidative phosphorylation. CONCLUSION: This integrated separation strategy enables efficient valorization of G. frondosa liquid by-products and clarifies the structure-activity relationship of LMWPP. The recycled natural LMWPP shows promise as a pediatric antiviral functional food ingredient, providing a feasible industrial approach for high-value reuse of edible fungal processing waste. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
journal: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture

title_zh: 灰树花加工副产物的价值:新型低分子量多糖肽的纯化、结构表征和抗 EV71 生物活性
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The large volume of supernatant generated during Grifola frondosa extraction is typically discarded, resulting in substantial resource waste and environmental pressure. Such agro-fungal processing by-products are rich in potentially bioactive macromolecules, but efficient recycling strategies and biofunctional verification remain limited. Meanwhile, safe natural antiviral ingredients for pediatric enterovirus infection are lacking. This study established a sustainable chromatographic bioprocess to recover a low-molecular-weight polysaccharide-peptide (LMWPP) from G. frondosa waste liquid, with the aims of achieving high-value circular utilization of fungal processing wastewater and exploring its anti-EV71 potential. RESULTS: Da possessed pyranose structures with α- and β-glycosidic bonds and consisted of multiple monosaccharides and leucine-dominant amino acids. Recovered LMWPP exerted marked anti-EV71 effects by mitigating cytotoxicity, inhibiting viral replication, downregulating VP1 mRNA expression, and alleviating cell apoptosis. Transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated its regulatory effects on the complement and coagulation cascades, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling, and oxidative phosphorylation. CONCLUSION: This integrated separation strategy enables efficient valorization of G. frondosa liquid by-products and clarifies the structure-activity relationship of LMWPP. The recycled natural LMWPP shows promise as a pediatric antiviral functional food ingredient, providing a feasible industrial approach for high-value reuse of edible fungal processing waste. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
abstract_zh: 背景:灰树花提取过程中产生的大量上清液通常被丢弃,造成大量资源浪费和环境压力。这种农业真菌加工副产品富含潜在的生物活性大分子,但有效的回收策略和生物功能验证仍然有限。同时,缺乏治疗儿童肠道病毒感染的安全天然抗病毒药物成分。本研究建立了一种可持续的色谱生物工艺,从灰树花废液中回收低分子量多糖肽(LMWPP),旨在实现真菌加工废水的高值循环利用并探索其抗EV71潜力。结果:Da具有α-和β-糖苷键的吡喃糖结构,由多个单糖和亮氨酸为主的氨基酸组成。恢复后的 LMWPP 通过减轻细胞毒性、抑制病毒复制、下调 VP1 mRNA 表达和减轻细胞凋亡来发挥显着的抗 EV71 作用。转录组分析进一步证明了其对补体和凝血级联、过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体(PPAR)信号传导和氧化磷酸化的调节作用。结论:这种集成分离策略能够有效地利用灰树花液体副产物,并阐明 LMWPP 的构效关系。回收的天然LMWPP显示出作为儿科抗病毒药物功能性食品成分的前景,为食用菌加工废物的高价值再利用提供了可行的工业方法。© 2026 中国化学工业学会。

title: Enhancing immunogenicity: Evaluating the polio antigen immune response in hexavalent vaccine formulations
abstract: Hexavalent vaccines simplify childhood immunization by combining antigens against six diseases in a single formulation; however, the immunogenicity of each component must be evaluated. This study assessed poliovirus-specific immunoglobulin G (IgG) responses elicited by candidate hexavalent vaccines containing different doses of Sabin strain-derived inactivated poliovirus vaccine (sIPV). A preclinical study was conducted using 40 Wistar rats allocated to five groups: hexavalent vaccine containing low-, medium-, or high-dose sIPV; pentavalent vaccine combined with sIPV; or adjuvant control. Each group comprised four male and four female rats. The animals received primary immunization at week 0 and booster doses at weeks 4 and 8. Serotype-specific IgG titers were measured at weeks 0, 4, 8, and 12 using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Antibody responses were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance. Titers against poliovirus serotypes 1, 2, and 3 were negligible at baseline and remained low at week 4. title: Single-amplicon RT-PCR and Illumina sequencing of rhinovirus and enterovirus genomes v1
abstract: This protocol amplifies the coding-complete genome of rhinoviruses and enteroviruses (approximately 7 kb) from extracted RNA in a single RT-PCR, using a 5′ UTR forward primer (f448) and a reverse primer that targets the tag introduced during reverse transcription with T30TAG, and prepares the product for Illumina sequencing. A visible band on an agarose gel before library preparation indicates successful amplification. In 140 rhinovirus-positive respiratory specimens, the protocol yielded genomic data from 84% of specimens, including six co-infections with two rhinovirus genotypes (of the same or different species) and one co-infection of rhinovirus with coxsackievirus. The protocol also recovered high-quality genomes of 26 enterovirus A–D types in a panel of 41 isolates.

full_text: AbstractFragment screens provide an information-rich starting point for designing derivative compounds in structure-based drug discovery. However, derivatives in the fragment-to-hit stage are typically designed from only one or a few fragments, risking premature convergence on an unproductive series and dramatically limiting exploration of the binding site's interaction opportunities. This is avoidable by exploring a broad, chemically diverse set of scaffolds and elaborations spanning interactions revealed across many fragments, as well as those not yet observed. Conventional catalog procurement makes this breadth of testing prohibitively expensive for early discovery. In-house high-throughput (HT) synthesis can raise interaction productivity, the number of unique predicted protein–ligand interactions achievable within a given budget, by lowering the cost per compound, including labor and consumables, yet no design tool exists for this purpose. We introduce Syndirella (Synthesis Directed Elaborations), which presents a candidate elaboration space around input fragment-derived scaffolds, constrained to HT-compatible reactions and catalog reactants, for cost-effective sampling of many scaffolds' elaborations in a single experimental cycle. Applied to three viral protein targets, Syndirella designs demonstrated pharmacophore diversity, recapitulating known fragment interactions, identifying novel functionally relevant ones, and accessing chemical space absent from commercial catalogs. A companion paper details validation on a calcium-binding protein, yielding crystallographic structures and measurable binding, with in-house synthesis achieving a 71% cost reduction over catalog purchasing, labor and consumables included. Reactant rather than product procurement gives potentially 2.5 times as many accessible compounds and higher interaction productivity for the same budget. Syndirella is most impactful for structure-enabled campaigns with fragment-bound crystal structures, robust HT chemistry, and assays compatible with crude reaction mixtures, and is available at https://github.com/oxpig/syndirella. Syndirella proposes elaborations of fragment-derived scaffolds for high-throughput synthesis using in-catalog reactants for SAR exploration. MethodsSyndirella takes as input fragment or fragment-derived scaffold structures and outputs congeneric series with 3D poses and associated synthetic routes suitable for HT synthesis. For each scaffold, synthetic routes are first solved using a retrosynthesis tool or defined manually, and for each required reactant, a superstructure search is performed under constraints that preserve the reaction site. The resulting reactant superstructures are combined to yield a large set of elaborated products, which are then energy-minimized in silico into the experimental protein structure with strong constraints to the experimental fragment pose using Fragmenstein.51 Predicted conformations are subsequently scored and filtered based on geometry checks and modeled binding energy. The pipeline is tunable and expandable to accommodate the specific capabilities and preferences of downstream HT synthesis experiments.Computational workflowSyndirella produces congeneric series of compounds from input scaffolds with fragment origin. These scaffolds can be fragments themselves or derivatives from fragment growing, linking, or most commonly in this work, fragment merges.52 Fragment merged compounds can be proposed algorithmically or manually, although design methods should prioritize the recapitulation of fragment atoms. One algorithmic method that implements fragment merging and is extensively used throughout our pipeline is Fragmenstein.51 Fragmenstein combines atoms from fragments using structural information to create derivatives that are predicted to adopt the same binding pose as the fragments. Additionally, Wills et al. utilized the Fragment Network,53,54 first described by Astex Pharmaceuticals,15 where traversing a graph database of compounds starting from a fragment node leads to derivative compounds that recapitulate fragment–protein interactions. Compounds that are used as input into the complete Syndirella workflow are hereafter referred to as scaffolds, shown in Fig. 1.Fig. 1Workflow of Syndirella starting from a fragment-inspired scaffold, the pipeline defines synthetic routes, identifies superstructures of reactants from chemical catalogs, predicts products via combinatorial synthesis, and performs placement relative to inspiration fragments using Fragmenstein.51 The example shows a two-step synthesis (amidation and Suzuki coupling) where final products (thick representation) are overlaid with original fragments (thin representation), with successful placements indicated by green checkmarks and not successful by red crosses.Pose generation of scaffolds and filteringFirst, poses are generated for input scaffolds to filter out those which do not have an energetically favorable conformation in the binding site. Pose generation is performed using the tool Fragmenstein,51 although any pose generation method could be used, whether restrained to the parent fragment pose or not. Fragmenstein generates an initial pose by calculating the positional overlap between the compound and fragments used for the original merge. The atoms on the compound found in this overlap are restricted to the coordinates from the fragments. This unphysical conformation undergoes energy minimization placed in the apo protein template specified by the user. Energy minimization is controlled by either PyRosetta's scorefunction ref2015 (ref. 55) or RDKit's UFF.56 For the analysis shown here, minimization with RDKit's UFF was performed unless specified otherwise. When using PyRosetta, the sidechains of protein residues with alpha carbons within 8 Å of the centroid of the compound are energy minimized whereas the protein is fixed when performing UFF minimization. A ΔΔG score is calculated by Fragmenstein as a single snapshot difference of the final bound state minus the unbound state (see ref. 51). It should be mentioned that this ΔΔG score should not be interpreted as a robust free binding energy and instead is used only as a filter where if the score is ≥0 the pose is most likely energetically unfavorable and strained.Scaffolds that complete energy minimization within 240 s, have an RMSD of <2 Å to the inspiration fragments, have a ΔΔG score of <0, and pass PoseBuster's intramolecular geometry checks for bond lengths, angles, steric clashes, and aromatic ring planarity are accepted.57Route modeling for HT synthesisFor each scaffold that passes pose generation, Syndirella proposes elaborations by explicit SMIRKS-encoded forward synthesis route modelling with any number of reaction steps.58 First, route selection is specified for the scaffold manually or proposed by a retrosynthesis tool. Here in this analysis using Manifold (https://postera.ai/), although functionality using the open-source tool AiZynthFinder is also provided. When using Manifold, the catalogs specified to query were enamine_bb, mcule, mcule_ultimate, enamine_real, enamine_made, and generic (common molecules that are found in most catalogs).59–61 For a compound to be considered “elaboratable”, there must be a forward synthesis route with all reactions encoded in Syndirella's SMIRKS library. Syndirella includes 109 SMIRKS encoded reactions which have been specifically chosen for HT chemistry. In this work 23 were used (available as RXN_SMIRKS_CONSTANTS.json on Zenodo62) and since this analysis, more have been added with a significant amount from Dobbelaere et al.63 and are found at https://github.com/oxpig/syndirella.Syndirella prioritizes user synthesis preferencesSyndirella's reaction repertoire can be expanded or edited by adding a SMIRKS pattern58 representing the reaction of interest (e.g., sourced from resources such as SMARTS-RX64 or SmartReact65). Additionally, reaction substitutions can be specified to suit user preferences based on better yield history or usually cheaper reactants. For example, replacing Schotten–Baumann reactions with amidations often improves building block availability and reduces cost (Fig. S4). Each alternative reaction generates an additional and separate synthesis route and can be specified in a .json format and example jupyter notebooks to generate these files are provided (see https://github.com/oxpig/syndirella).Superstructure search of reactants to produce elaborated productsTo produce the series, each reactant in the forward synthesis route is elaborated and the full Cartesian product of the reactants is computed in silico. The following steps are taken for each reaction step in the forward synthesis route. First, the original reactants are labeled with the specific reactant number in the SMIRKS of that reaction. Then, each reactant is used as a query in a superstructure search – performed by Manifold in this work, although functionality using the catalog search tool Arthor (https://arthor.docking.org/) is provided. A superstructure of a query compound is a compound that contains the query compound as a maximum common substructure. In this analysis, the catalogs queried were enamine_bb, mcule, mcule_ultimate, enamine_real, enamine_made, and generic (common molecules that are found in most catalogs).59–61Superstructure reactants are filtered by removing duplicates, compounds containing non-abundant isotopes, compounds that don't match the reactant SMIRKS, and if the number of atom difference to the query reactant is <0 or >10 (although these thresholds can be changed to user preferences). If the step is a bimolecular reaction, reactants that contain both reacting groups are excluded to reduce selectivity issues.Product compounds are generated from the full Cartesian product of the smallest 100 reactants for bimolecular reactions or by the smallest 10 K reactants for unimolecular reactions, thereby restricting the total number of products in each step to ≤10 K (although this threshold can be changed to user preferences). For each reactant combination, the product is determined by the original SMIRKS reaction pattern. Products are excluded if they cannot be sanitized by the RDKit.66 If multiple products are produced for a single combination, the product is flagged with a selectivity issue label.The previous steps repeat for each reaction step until the final products are determined and labeled with their InChi key and ordered in ascending atom count. All stereoisomers are enumerated and the SMILES and full routes are stored as a dataframe.67,68Pose generation of products and filteringEach compound must be placed into the protein pocket to predict the interactions between the compound and residues. The smallest 10 K elaborations after stereo enumeration are placed and filtered following the same steps detailed above for scaffold placement, although this threshold can be changed to user preferences.XChem data setsThe three test cases used in this work are publicly available crystallographic fragment screens from the XChem facility,69,70 summarized in Table 1 and are available for download from the Fragalysis platform (https://fragalysis.diamond.ac.uk). Scaffolds from these datasets were derived from three sources: computational fragment merging algorithms (either Knitwork53,54 or Fragmenstein51), exact fragment hits, or manually designed fragment merges.Table 1Summary of scaffolds used as test dataTargetOriginCountUnique fragment combinationsChikungunya virus nsP3 macrodomain (CHIKV-Mac)Fragmenstein317616Manual14 Total 331 Coxsackievirus A16 2A protease (EV-A71-2A)Exact348Knitwork42Manual76 Total 121 Enterovirus D68 3C protease (EV-D68-3C-PROA)Knitwork29158 Total 291 The Chikungunya virus nsP3 macrodomain protein (CHIKV-Mac) performs removal of ADP-ribose modifications to host proteins, an essential part of the replication process for Chikungunya virus.71 It has been shown mutants affecting ADP–ribose binding slows viral replication in mammalian cells and reduces virulence.72 A fragment screen was performed, resulting in 66 fragments bound in the ADP–ribose binding site and 616 unique combinations were used to design scaffolds by Fragmenstein and Knitwork.73Enterovirus A71 is a common cause of respiratory disease and hand, foot, and mouth disease in children worldwide.74 The 2A protease (EV-A71-2A) is responsible for a single intramolecular cleavage in the viral polyprotein, therefore targeting the active site could inhibit viral growth. Following a fragment screen on Coxsackievirus A16 2A protease which serves as a proxy for the highly conserved EV-A71-2A protein, 43 fragments were resolved in the active site and a variety of follow-up methods were utilized including manual designs to result in 121 scaffolds.75Similar to enterovirus A71, enterovirus D68 results in respiratory illness and in severe cases, paralysis.76 The 3C protease (EV-D68-3C) is required to cleave the non-structural part of the viral polyprotein. EV-D68-3C also cleaves many host proteins to facilitate viral infection thus, inhibition can reduce the viral replication by this target. The fragment screen of this target resulted in 16 fragments resolved in the active site, and only the Knitwork tool was used to propose 291 scaffolds.77All scaffolds input into the pipeline totaled to 743, hereafter referred to as the original-743. After inputting into Syndirella, successful series were defined as having >3 unique products and >0 successful placements of elaborations, totaling to 234, hereafter referred to as the successful-234 (Fig. S1).Cheminformatic analysisMorgan fingerprints with a radius of three and bit length of 2048 were used for all fingerprinting calculations using the RDKit.66,78 For the per cluster analysis, the mean Tanimoto values were calculated by taking the row-wise mean across the full Tanimoto similarity matrix for each elaboration in the cluster against all other molecules. Histograms of the mean Tanimoto values per cluster and smoothed by kernel density estimation using Seaborn's default parameters were calculated.79 All displays of chemical space by two dimensions were carried out by calculating the 50 first components from principal component decomposition of the Morgan fingerprints then transforming those components using the t-SNE algorithm. These transformations were carried out using the default parameters in scikit-learn.80R-group decomposition was carried out with the RDKit's RGroupDecompose function where the cores required to identify the R positions were the input scaffolds used.66 Then the R groups were filtered by removing repeats across all R positions and those with more than one attachment point. R-group pharmacophores were assigned per atom using the RDKit66 using the following custom rules. Hydrophobic, carbon with no N/O/S neighbour. Hydrogen bond donor (HBD), N or O bearing ≥1 hydrogen. Hydrogen bond acceptor (HBA), N or O bearing no hydrogen, or a neutral NH. Halogen, F/Cl/Br/I. Classes are non-exclusive. Each R group was summarized by the shortest topological (bond count) distance from the attachment point at which each class occurred, giving one pharmacophore-distance pair per class per R group.For the missing chemistry analysis, the original-743 were queried by Postera's Manifold for the top five retrosynthesis routes ordered by Manifold using the same catalogues as in Syndirella's default pipeline specifications.Comparison to traditional superstructure methodsThe scaffolds used as input for Arthor (https://arthor.docking.org/) and Manifold superstructure querying were a subset of the original-743 that passed placement filtered by the same constraints as described in the Computational workflow filtering section, resulting in 660 scaffolds, hereafter referred to as the scaffold-pass-660 (Fig. S1).
